display: Paper conservator at a university library in New York, trained in Western paper and parchment. I'm looking for East Asian mounting expertise for a donated collection of about 300 Chinese stone rubbings and two albums.

signals.text: I'm looking for someone trained in East Asian paper conservation (China, Japan or Taiwan) to work on a donated collection of Chinese rubbings.
About 300 Chinese stone rubbings and two albums have come into our library. Several pieces have flaking paste and silverfish damage.
The paste on these rubbings flakes in a way I don't recognise from Western starch, and I want to learn what it is.
The albums are the priority. They are accordion-folded with tipped-in sheets, and one has pages mended with cellophane tape.
Western conservation conferences have almost nothing on East Asian rubbings. I'm looking for the community, courses or workshops that cover them.
The donor hopes to see the collection exhibited next spring, so I need to know how long treatment realistically takes and who could do it.
I've catalogued about 60 items and photographed about 30. I'd like help cataloguing and reading the inscriptions, colophons and calligraphy.
I'd like to invite a specialist to work with us in person for a short residency, which my department could support.
I'm after introductions to East Asian mounting specialists more than general advice. I'd rather ask carefully than send a broad call for help.
I need a way to learn East Asian mounting techniques myself, so the library can care for these items after a specialist leaves.
My schedule is tight, and my home life limits how far I can travel.

offers.text: A fully equipped paper conservation lab (fume hood, suction table, humidification chamber, light table) that a visiting specialist could use.
Eleven years of hands-on conservation of Western rag paper, parchment and early printed books.
Training in Japanese tissue mending and wheat starch paste, including surface cleaning, mould treatment and deacidification.
Access to the library's special collections catalogue and cataloguers, so a collaborator's findings can be properly recorded.
Pest management experience with insect-damaged paper, including freezing treatment for silverfish.
A network of American paper conservators, including colleagues in Manhattan.
A possible exhibition venue and a donor who wants these items shown, which could give a collaborator public credit for the work.
A funded visiting-specialist slot covering travel, accommodation and a day rate, available until 30 June.
I play viola in a community orchestra and can bring music and company to anyone who joins.

catchers.hypo: I trained in East Asian scroll and album mounting in Taiwan. I'm in the US and looking for conservation work on Chinese rubbings.
catchers.can: Discuss the collection's condition and timeline, and consider a paid visit through the department's visiting-specialist fund.
catchers.confirm: Were you trained in East Asian mounting (paste, backing papers and mounting sequence), not only Western paper conservation?

catchers.hypo: I know a mounting master in Shanghai who would enjoy working on old rubbings, but she doesn't speak English well.
catchers.can: Describe the project, then share the condition report and photographs so the master can assess the work.
catchers.confirm: Has this person actually mounted or repaired Chinese rubbings or albums, rather than only scrolls or paintings?

catchers.hypo: I'm a graduate student in East Asian art history. I'd love to help catalogue and read the inscriptions on a donated rubbing collection.
catchers.can: Bring them to the library's catalogue and cataloguers, and compare their identifications with the 60 items already catalogued.
catchers.confirm: Can you read classical Chinese inscriptions and colophons on rubbings?

catchers.hypo: Our museum has an album with flaking paste and old tape repairs. How did you stabilise yours before treatment?
catchers.can: Share what I've learned about freezing, documentation and stabilising the albums, and compare notes.
catchers.confirm: Is the object an East Asian album or rubbing with flaking paste, tape repairs or insect damage?

catchers.hypo: I'm a conservator in Manhattan and I know a couple of East Asian specialists. Would you like an introduction?
catchers.can: Follow through on the introductions that my Met colleague has offered to arrange, and send a short project brief ahead.
catchers.confirm: Do you know someone who personally treated East Asian paper, and can you pass on a first message?

catchers.hypo: I run special collections at another university. We have Chinese rubbings nobody can treat, and I'd like to share a specialist.
catchers.can: Compare notes on specialist time and costs, and perhaps share a visiting specialist across institutions through Marjorie and the department.
catchers.confirm: Does your institution hold East Asian rubbings or albums that need treatment now?

catchers.hypo: I'm a violist new to New York, and I'm looking for a friendly amateur orchestra.
catchers.can: Invite them to the Saturday rehearsal of my community orchestra, where the viola section is four players.
catchers.confirm: Do you play viola at an amateur level and have time for weekly rehearsals?

catchers.hypo: I'm a vet tech who has managed diabetic cats on insulin schedules. Would you like some tips or cat-sitting?
catchers.can: Consider help with twice-daily insulin so I can travel, or advice on keeping a routine.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally given insulin injections to a cat on a 7am and 7pm schedule?

forbids.text: I can't travel for more than one day at a time.
No treatment involving chemicals that could harm paper.
I won't let anyone treat the albums without a documented plan and the library's approval.
I don't talk about my personal finances.
Funds can only be spent on a visiting specialist, within the fund's terms and before 30 June.

projects.name: Chinese rubbings and albums
projects.text: Conserve and catalogue a donated collection of about 300 Chinese stone rubbings and two albums for exhibition next spring.

projects.name: Visiting specialist residency
projects.text: A funded short visit in which a specialist works alongside me in the lab to assess and begin treatment of the albums.

policy.t1: With a real sign of interest, I'll share the condition of the items, the damage found so far, and the timeline.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and the person is clear, I'll share the visiting-specialist fund, its terms and its deadline.
policy.never: My personal finances, my household costs, or any claim that I can't handle the collection.
